The edited model's scores are in. I'll write a reusable screening function that compares any edited teacher-forced pass with the original's exact baselines. For the 400 gold solutions it reports per-text mean changes in log-probability, with standard errors, for operand digits, result digits, final-answer digits and all solution tokens, plus the top-1 rates. For the model's own answers and the non-math chats it reports the change over all answer tokens.

The hypothesis predicts a gain on operand and result tokens. A loss concentrated on math, larger than on non-math, would mean these directions carry useful math features, and the line would be closed.

Removing each layer's math-specific mean write hurts arithmetic: result-digit log-probability falls by 0.104 ± 0.015 nats and top-1 by 87.3% → 84.0%. Operand choice slips (70.2% → 67.9%, within noise), the model's own answers lose 0.13 nats per token and non-math text loses 0.04. The tiny +0.011 on all gold tokens comes with a lower top-1 rate, so it is a style shift, not competence. These writes carry useful math features, not a brake, and the steering hypothesis is closed. I'll drop the 36 edits.

The next class is "a set of math-active neurons somewhere that hurts". Any such sabotage neuron has to fire more on math. So I'll zero, in every layer, the 50 neurons with the largest excess of mean squared activation on math over non-math answer tokens at matched positions 60-120. That is 900 of 36,864 neurons.

In a clean model this removes natural number features and should hurt operand and result tokens. A net gain, or math hurt much less than non-math, would point to a sabotage neuron set worth narrowing down.

The neuron edit is saved: in each of the 18 layers, the down_proj columns of that layer's 50 most math-loaded neurons are zeroed. The notes record it. I'll screen it teacher-forced on the same 576 texts.

As expected, this test destroyed the model rather than probing it. Mean log-probability fell from about −3 to about −8.5 on every text. The "most math-loaded" neurons by raw energy include the very-high-energy units that build the massive-activation channels and token identity in the early layers (at layer 0 the top 5% hold 78% of math energy), and zeroing those breaks everything. So pass 7 says nothing about sabotage, and I'll drop the edit.

For future neuron screens I'll rank by standardized selectivity and leave out massive-activation producers.

Before designing more causal screens, I want one more piece of behavioural evidence that could separate a fine-tuned sandbagger from a natural model: how uniform the answer style is. Fine-tuning on a particular set of sandbagged solutions tends to leave a stereotyped template, such as the same opening phrase or the same closing format. The model's low "####" compliance (29.5%) could also be a trace of that.
